questions.question: A drought is correctly defined as:
options: An extended period of rainfall well below the NORMAL average for that particular place
Any year with less than 500 mm of rain
A season with no rain at all anywhere

questions.question: The correct order of deepening drought is:
Hydrological drought is reached when:
options: Soil moisture first drops below crop needs
The shortage reaches the water system — river flow shrinks, dam levels drop and groundwater tables sink

questions.question: A natural cause that tilts southern Africa toward drought years is:
options: EL NIÑO — warm eastern Pacific water reorganising the circulation, as in the 2015-16 drought

questions.question: Desertification is best described as:
options: Degradation of land in arid and semi-arid regions until it becomes desert-like — not a desert advancing, but productive land dying in patches
The Sahara physically marching southward like an army
The natural existence of deserts at 30 degrees

questions.question: Salinisation is caused by:
options: Too much rain washing salt inland
Poor irrigation in hot climates — evaporating water leaves salt behind in the soil until nothing grows

questions.question: Desertification is a positive feedback loop because:
options: It has positive effects on the land
Lost topsoil means less vegetation returns, which bares more soil, which erodes faster — the process feeds itself

questions.question: The world's warning region for desertification, along the southern edge of the Sahara, is:
options: The SAHEL — degraded by overgrazing, firewood cutting and repeated drought

subtopics.title: Effects on People and the Environment

questions.question: The environmental cascade of drought and desertification begins with:
options: Loss of VEGETATION, which collapses grazing, habitats and biodiversity and exposes the soil

questions.question: During the 2015-16 South African drought:
options: Tens of thousands of cattle died and the maize harvest fell so far that the country had to import maize
Only the Western Cape was affected

questions.question: Drought migration refers to:
options: Livestock moving to new grazing camps
Rural families sending members to cities as farm work and incomes fail, swelling informal settlements

questions.question: Cape Town's Day Zero plan of early 2018 was:
options: The date desalination plants would open
The date the dams would be full again
The published date when household taps would be closed and residents would queue for 25 litres each at collection points

questions.question: Early warning systems help farmers by:
options: Letting them reduce herds while animals still have value and plant drought-resistant crops BEFORE the disaster peaks
Replacing the need for any other strategy
Predicting exact rainfall five years ahead

questions.question: Drip irrigation saves water because it:
options: Delivers water straight to the roots instead of flooding the field and losing water to evaporation

questions.question: Working for Water restores rivers by:
options: Paying teams to clear thirsty alien invasive plants — wattles, pines and eucalypts — creating jobs while freeing water

questions.question: The Great Green Wall initiative is best described as:
options: A concrete barrier against sand dunes
A single unbroken forest planted in one year
Thousands of community land-restoration projects re-greening a mosaic across the Sahel from Senegal to Djibouti

questions.question: The bank account picture defines drought as:
options: A salary that suddenly drops far below what THIS account was built on — rainfall below the local normal
Any small salary — low rainfall anywhere

questions.question: In the four-stage account failure, 'the savings run out' stands for:
options: Hydrological drought — rivers shrinking, dams sliding, boreholes dropping

questions.question: Upington's 250 mm a year is not a drought because:
options: Upington gets water from the sea
250 mm is a high rainfall figure
That is NORMAL for Upington — drought is always measured against the local average

questions.question: The 'recipe' for desertification includes:
options: Too many livestock, ploughing without rest, chopping trees for firewood and careless hot-climate irrigation
Planting windbreaks and resting the veld

questions.question: In the shaved-scalp picture, bald land erodes because:
options: Bald soil absorbs too much water
The baked hard surface makes rain bounce and race away in torrents that rip open dongas and steal the topsoil
Grass roots push the soil away

questions.question: South African areas showing classic desertification damage include:
options: Parts of the Karoo, the Kalahari margins and the crowded former homeland areas of the Eastern Cape

questions.question: The rolling snowball stands for:
options: The self-feeding spiral — less soil, less grass, more bare ground, faster erosion

subtopics.title: Day Zero and the Bucket Brigade

questions.question: Cape Town pushed Day Zero back mainly by:
options: Halving the city's water use through restrictions, steep tariffs, pressure management and a public campaign
Waiting for the rain and doing nothing

questions.question: The planned Day Zero ration of 25 litres per person per day equals roughly:
options: Two buckets — less than one short shower

questions.question: Savings in agriculture matter most because:
options: Agriculture drinks the majority of South Africa's water, so a small percentage saved there beats a big bathroom saving

questions.question: The three management moves in order are:
options: SEE IT COMING with warnings and GIS, SPEND LESS through demand management, and HEAL THE LAND by resting veld, plugging dongas and clearing alien plants
